IF THE DESK STOPS

Check before acting.

Check the record, then check the physical stock.

01 / DEMO SCOPE

Practice in this tab

This website simulates the desk entirely in browser memory. It has no Python server, shared database, staff authentication, durable audit or production code security. Reloading or closing the tab loses all changes. Different devices have separate demo inventories. Never use it to manage real passes.

02 / UNCERTAIN HANDOVER

Reserved is not handed over

A recorded release already subtracts its quantities from the balance. The original operator must inspect physical stock and the recorded categories. Hand over those reserved passes only once, or confirm if already handed over. If uncertain, stop and involve a supervisor. No automatic return, replacement, reset or undo.

03 / SHARING THE CODE

Show or tell the code privately

Show the private code on screen or read it quietly in three groups. Ask the depositor to repeat it back before closing, then have them share it with trusted friends. No printed receipt is needed. Anyone holding it can collect any remaining passes; it does not assign a quantity to a friend. This hosted demo only previews sharing text locally. It does not ask for phone numbers, open WhatsApp or send messages. Never write the code on a publicly visible envelope.

NFC: future option only. Not implemented or tested here. Desktop Chrome does not support Web NFC; supported Android tag workflows are not phone-to-phone sharing. Use private on-screen or verbal sharing instead. No offline NFC promise.

04 / BEFORE REAL USE

A demo is not the live desk

A real event needs one authoritative custody service, authenticated staff, durable transactions, secure code verification, supervised recovery and device testing. A browser-local demo cannot prevent duplicate collection across tabs or devices. No admission validation, backup, offline installation or production deployment is provided here.

Demo boundaries

One browser tab. Use synthetic data only. This simulation is not secure storage. No default ID check, named collectors, individual allocation, remote synchronization, admission validation or code-replacement workflow. Staff labels and original-operator checks are procedural, not authentication. A lost code requires supervisor review outside this demo; packet ID alone cannot authorize release.
